column1: # Hand-authored whole-sentence cases. Unlike the word set, these are not in any dictionary as a
# single entry, so answering them requires segmentation plus assembly — which is what the word
# lattice and the fallback decoder actually do.
# Gold is the one natural writing a native reader would produce for the pinyin as given. Cases
# whose pinyin genuinely admits two equally natural writings were not included: an eval set cannot
# be honest and ambiguous at the same time.
# Twelve cases break that rule and are now tagged `pronoun-ambiguous`. They open with ta, and
# 他/她/它 are indistinguishable in pinyin, so with nothing before them there is no correct answer
# to find — a scorer can only follow its corpus prior. All twelve have 他 as the gold, which is the
# author's habit rather than a fact about the pinyin, and a model trained on a corpus where 他
# outnumbers 她 collects those twelve for free. They are kept rather than deleted because that is
# worth being able to see: report with and without the tag, and the difference is the prior.
# n=60. The 95% confidence half-width on a single proportion at this size is roughly 13 points, so
# aggregate movement here is not evidence on its own. Compare runs case by case, using the rank of
# each gold answer, not by differencing the summary numbers.
# No real personal data: every name is a common surname plus a generic given name.
